transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Time: 20:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Priya Sinha (Redwood SE), Mark Alvarez (CTO - Northgate), Jules Carter (Senior Infra Engineer - Northgate), Lina Gomez (Security Architect - Northgate)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Northgate's constraints for a Private VPC deployment of Redwood: networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink / interface endpoints), region constraints (primary in us-west-2, DR in eu-west-1), egress/NAT cost concerns, KMS integrations and audit log forwarding. Team requested architecture diagram, pricing scenarios, and a technical deep-dive with cloud ops.

Topics:
- VPC peering vs PrivateLink
- Private endpoints and DNS routing
- Region constraints and replication
- Data residency and audit logs
- KMS/HSM and envelope encryption
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Daniel (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm daniel from redwood, i think we have about 50 minutes, quick intros?
[00:06] Mark (CTO): hi Mark here, CTO at northgate. Jules and Lina are on to cover infra and security.
[00:12] Jules: hey all, Jules - i'm our infra lead, we'll be the ones touching vpc stuff.
[00:16] Lina: Lina, security architect, SOC2/compliance owner.
[00:20] Priya (SE): hi i'm priya, i'll dive into the network pieces and feasibility.
[00:25] Daniel: great, objective today is to understand your constraints for private deployment - are you leaning private because of data residency or network isolation?
[00:34] Mark: primarily isolation, we move manifests and manifests.. sorry, we move PII-ish logistics data and need no public egress; also compliance - SOC2 and internal audits. we also have latency SLAs for certain routing decisions.
[00:48] Jules: additional constraint - our workloads run in us-west-2, but leadership wants a DR region in eu-west-1. we need to understand if redwood can colocate inference in us-west-2 and failover to eu-west-1 without cross-region data residency issues.
[01:05] Priya: yeah that's common; we support region-specific deployments. For private mode we can deploy control plane in a customer-managed VPC or provide private endpoints, depends on which pattern you prefer. question - do you want full control plane in your VPC or 'private endpoints' back to Redwood-managed infra?
[01:22] Mark: ideally full control plane in our VPC or an appliance; but we also want to avoid managing GPUs on prem. so something in our cloud account under our VPC is preferred.
[01:33] Daniel: okay so agent is expecting Private (VPC) deployment where we run the Redwood private control plane in your account and we either run dedicated GPUs in your VPC or in a dedicated subnet - many customers take that route.
[01:46] Lina: important: KMS integration must use our CMKs; keys must not be accessible from Redwood's account. is that doable?
[01:54] Priya: yes we support customer-managed KMS keys; we can show HSM/KMS patterns — essentially the worker nodes access ciphertext via IAM roles in your account, keys never leave your control.
[02:05] Jules: ok sweet. on networking - peering versus PrivateLink - we worry about CIDR overlap with partner networks and transitive routing.
[02:14] Priya: right so quick break down — VPC peering is straightforward but does not support transitive routing; if you have many spokes that can be messy. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives you an elastic network interface in your subnet and simplifies routing plus the endpoint is private. Peering tends to be cheaper for heavy egress but PrivateLink is more secure & SAML friendly for some customers.
[02:35] Mark: cost is a thing - NAT gateway egress costs blow up with high token throughput, do you have guidance on expected egress patterns for inference?
[02:44] Daniel: yes, inference is mostly egress token traffic; with private deployment the traffic stays inside the cloud region between your app and the workers if colocated, so NAT egress to public internet is minimal unless you call external services. We'll include estimated bandwidth numbers in the pricing doc.
[02:56] Jules: if we colocate in our VPC, is data plane traffic between our app and the Redwood workers local? what about cross AZ?
[03:05] Priya: data plane will be in your VPC and across AZs within the region; we recommend pinned subnets for low latency. Cross-region replication for cache or model artifacts is optional and we can control what data moves across regions.
[03:20] Lina: audit trail question - can you forward application-level logs and inference audit events to our CloudWatch or to an S3 bucket in our account?
[03:29] Daniel: yes, we can push logs to your account. For private deployments we typically configure a logging role so logs and audit events land in your CloudWatch/S3; we'll provide example IAM policies.
[03:40] Mark: on the topic of endpoints - DNS resolution and split-horizon, how do you handle service discovery for internal endpoints? we can't have public DNS entries.
[03:49] Priya: we can either integrate with your Route53 private hosted zones or provide hostnames via the VPC endpoint. We'll include DNS setup steps in the playbook; also suggest keeping short TTLs during rollouts.
[04:03] Jules: about peering - we have overlapping CIDR ranges with a partner in a different account, so peering is tricky. PrivateLink seems safer. Any downsides?
[04:12] Priya: PrivateLink tends to have per-GB charges for data processed and hourly endpoint costs; peering is more straightforward for east-west traffic. We'll run a cost comparison for your throughput – that's part of the action items.
[04:24] Mark: what about model updates and artifacts? do those need internet egress to pull images?
[04:30] Daniel: models can be stored in your private S3 and we support pulling from customer buckets via roles; otherwise we can stage artifacts in a private bucket in your account. Model pull can be configured to use VPC endpoints so no internet egress is necessary.
[04:45] Lina: encryption in transit and at rest? are we covered if we use our CMKs?
[04:50] Priya: yes, TLS for in transit; at rest we can encrypt with your CMKs. For KV caches we offer envelope encryption patterns and the keys are in your account.
[04:59] Jules: what about network latency? our SLA wants 100ms p95 for certain calls, is that realistic?
[05:05] Daniel: depends on model size and batching. With colocated workers and pinned subnets we routinely see low tens of ms for small models; for larger models or heavy batching p95 will increase. We'll help size a dedicated pool to meet your latency targets.
[05:20] Mark: service accounts and RBAC - do we get SAML/SCIM integration and per-route permissions?
[05:26] Priya: yes SSO with SAML + SCIM provisioning supported. RBAC can be enforced at route and model level, and audit logs track token usage.
[05:36] Lina: compliance: we need SOC2 reports and a data flow diagram for auditors.
[05:42] Daniel: we'll share our SOC2 attestation and a redwood-private security pack; for customer-specific diagrams we'll annotate the architecture we provide.
[05:51] Mark: pilot scope - what would a 6-week pilot look like?
[05:56] Priya: typical pilot: week 1-2 network setup & VPC endpoints, week 3 infra warmup & model staging, week 4-5 performance benchmark with your prompts, week 6 finalize runbook and cutover plan. Success criteria: p95 latency under 100ms for small models, throughput X req/s, no public egress for data plane.
[06:17] Jules: ok sounds good. on quotas - how do we handle bursting? we use spiky workloads.
[06:22] Daniel: Dedicated capacity + autoscaling policies handle spikes; we can provision buffer capacity and set burst policies.
[06:29] Mark: any red flags or blockers from your side?
[06:32] Priya: main blocker is getting the VPC CIDRs, account IDs, and confirmation on whether you prefer PrivateLink or a full control-plane in your account. Also we need confirmation on CMK usage.
[06:44] Lina: i'll need an initial architecture to show our auditors, so please make that a priority.
[06:48] Daniel: absolutely. we'll send architecture + network playbook and pricing; priya will run the tech feasibility and we'll schedule the deep-dive.
[06:58] Mark: cool, thanks everyone. that's it from our side.
[07:02] Daniel: thanks all, recap and we'll follow up with docs and dates.

End of transcript.
